findings.text: ABC Type 42 is a non-quota on-sale beer-and-wine license for public premises (bar, wine bar, taproom) where no food is required and no minors are allowed. ABC issues new Type 42 licenses directly, but nearly every city treats a Type 42 as a bar use requiring a conditional use permit or planning review before ABC will issue.

The Third Street Alcohol RUD § 249.62(a)(2)(E) allows a new Type 42 establishment to open in the Bayview NCD with Conditional Use Authorization, but the rule does not define what makes an establishment new versus a transfer. The description does not state whether the license will be a new application or a transfer, so this control is not decided.

findings.text: Every food or drink business in San Francisco needs a DPH health permit to operate, issued after the final inspection confirms the facility matches approved plans and a certified food safety manager is on staff. The FY 2026-27 fee is $470 for the permit application including initial inspection, with a $0 annual license fee for restaurants and bars through 2026-28.

Limited cooking (small plates, light food preparation) requires DPH plan review of kitchen layout, equipment, finishes and menu. The FY 2026-27 flat fee for a bar with prepackaged food or limited prep is $1,241 for 4.5 hours of review, with additional review billed at $276 per hour.

A bar is Assembly Group A-2; a space for fewer than 50 people is Group B.

findings.text: Planning approved this address in 2019 as a grocery store with accessory wine-making and food prep, explicitly prohibiting bar or restaurant use with seating. Whether that grocery use is still active or the space is vacant is not shown by the records.

A change from grocery to bar is a Planning Code change of use. A change from Group B (grocery, or bar with fewer than 50 people) to Group A-2 (bar with 50 or more occupants) is a Building Code change of occupancy. Either change of use or change of occupancy triggers a building permit with plans routed to Planning for zoning review.

filing_playbook.action: Submit a written inquiry to SF Planning asking: (1) whether the space's last permitted use (2019 grocery store) triggers a Planning Code change of use to Bar, and (2) whether a new Type 42 license application will be treated as a new establishment under Third Street Alcohol RUD § 249.62(a)(2)(E).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Attach the 2016 wine bar approval (2016-002128MIS), the 2019 grocery approval (2019-003896MIS) and the 2020 Type 20 referral (2020-012156MIS) and ask Planning to confirm in writing: Is returning to a wine bar use at 5299 3rd St a Planning Code change of use requiring a Conditional Use Authorization under § 737 and § 249.62? Does § 249.62(a)(2)(E) treat a new Type 42 license application as a new establishment, or can the 2016 approval be relied upon? Request a pre-application meeting with the Conditional Use planner assigned to the Bayview district to walk through the site history and the Third Street RUD controls before filing.

filing_playbook.action: Form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State and obtain an EIN from the IRS.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File LLC Articles of Organization (Form LLC-1, $70) or incorporate (Form ARTS-GS, $100) with the CA Secretary of State online. File the Statement of Information within 90 days ($20 for an LLC). Apply for an Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the IRS online immediately after forming the entity; the EIN is issued the same day and is required for the bank account and ABC application. If operating under the DBA Gratta Wines, file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the SF County Clerk, publish once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper, and file proof of publication within 45 days.

filing_playbook.action: Register for the SF Business Registration Certificate and the CA Seller's Permit, and obtain workers' compensation insurance before filing the Conditional Use Authorization.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register with the SF Treasurer & Tax Collector for a Business Registration Certificate ($55-$700 based on gross receipts plus $4 state fee) to obtain your Business Account Number (BAN); every other city permit requires it. Register online with the CA Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA) for a Seller's Permit (free, often issued the same day); ABC will not issue a license until the seller's permit exists. Obtain workers' compensation insurance from a licensed carrier or State Fund before the first employee is hired; several city permits ask for proof of coverage. Register as an employer with the CA Employment Development Department (EDD) within 15 days of paying wages; your payroll provider needs the EDD account number.

filing_playbook.action: Submit building permit plans for tenant improvements (limited kitchen, restrooms, ADA upgrades) to DBI with the kitchen layout, equipment and finishes routed to DPH for health plan review.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Hire an architect experienced with SF restaurant and bar projects to prepare stamped plans showing the 1,200-square-foot layout with 40 seats, limited kitchen (prep sink, refrigeration, small cooking equipment), handwashing sinks, three-compartment sink, grease interceptor (if required by SFPUC's FOG program), ADA-compliant restrooms, and accessible path of travel. Submit the building permit application to DBI. DBI will route the plans to DPH for health plan review. DPH's plan-check fee for a bar with limited prep is $1,241 (FY 2026-27).

filing_playbook.action: After the building permit is issued and construction is substantially complete, schedule the DPH pre-opening inspection and obtain the health permit to operate.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Contact your DPH plan reviewer to schedule a pre-final inspection. Walk the space against the DPH checklist one week before the inspection: confirm hot water is working, handwashing sinks are stocked with soap and paper towels, all surfaces are sealed and smooth, food equipment is NSF-listed, and the three-compartment sink and grease interceptor are installed. Ensure at least one employee has passed an ANSI-accredited Certified Food Protection Manager exam (ServSafe or equivalent, $100-$250, valid 5 years) and all employees have California Food Handler Cards ($7-$15, valid 3 years). After the final inspection passes, DPH will issue the health permit to operate ($470 application fee, $0 annual license fee for 2026-28). timeline_cost.notes: The time and cost ranges cover the Conditional Use Authorization hearing (120-300 days from filing to approval, $3,100-$15,000 in Planning fees depending on construction cost) and the health permit to operate (14-45 days, $470 application fee plus $828-$1,241 for plan review). These are the approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted. The ranges do not include the ABC Type 42 license (60-150 days, $1,000-$1,600, handled in parallel after CUA approval), the building permit (14-120 days for plan review and construction, $800-$15,000 depending on scope), state and federal registrations (1-35 days, $200-$400 total), or sign and music licenses (7-45 days, $600-$5,000). The CUA timeline assumes no discretionary review requests or appeals; neighbor opposition or a discretionary review can add 3-6 months. If the census tract shows undue concentration of ABC licenses, a Public Convenience or Necessity letter from the Board of Supervisors may be required, adding 1-3 months to the ABC timeline. Start the CUA application at least 6 months before the target opening date. The total elapsed time from filing the CUA to opening the doors, including construction and all approvals, is typically 10-15 months for a new bar in San Francisco.

records_summary: The records show 5299 3rd St is within the Bayview Neighborhood Commercial District (NCD-BAYVIEW) and the Third Street Alcohol Restricted Use District. Under the current zoning rules a bar with an ABC Type 42 license is a conditional use here, requiring a Conditional Use Authorization. Critically, the Third Street Alcohol RUD at § 249.62(a)(2)(E) allows a new Type 42 establishment in the Bayview NCD only with Conditional Use approval. This address has recent history as Gratta Wines: in 2016 a wine bar was approved as accessory to Butchertown Gourmet restaurant, and in 2019-2020 the space transitioned to a grocery/wine-making use with a Type 20 off-sale license referral approved. Within 500 ft there is one active Type 41 license and one revoked Type 48 license; six registered food/drink businesses including four bars sit within 500 ft, signaling existing alcohol density on this block.
